newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus president appoints new cabinet.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus president appoints new cabinet.

text.p: Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides replaced five out of eleven ministers in his cabinet on Tuesday in a move described as a "renewal" of the centre-right government less than a year before a presidential election.
An official statement said that among the five new appointees, former government spokesman Yiannakis Cassoulides was named as the foreign minister to replace Alecos Michaelides.

The ministries of justice, education, health and communications were also given to new appointees, while all other ministers, including finance, kept their posts. The swearing-in ceremony was due to take place on Wednesday morning.
The reshuffle was widely expected and was the first since Clerides's election for a five-year term in 1993.
Political analyst Sofronis Sofroniou said the reshuffle could be an attempt by Clerides to reassert his influence within the Democratic Rally party.
"In the least he would have some of his people in key positions," Sofroniou added.

Clerides, a veteran right-wing politician, founded the Democratic Rally party in 1976. Although he remains honourary president of the party, his relations with key members has cooled significantly in recent months.

The party, split into "presidential" and "non-presidential" sympathisers, is due to hold elections in early June. Incumbent leader Yiannakis Matsis, who falls into the latter category, has accused Clerides of repeatedly ignoring the party that got him elected.
Government officials did not link the reshuffle to any need of the government to spruce up its image to boost Clerides's chances for re-election if he decided to run again.

Clerides himself also did not elaborate on the reasons for the reshuffle either. "It is simple. I wanted a renewal of the council of ministers, (cabinet)" he said in brief comments to reporters on the steps of the presidential palace.

Former foreign minister Michaelides's family firm owns a string of hotels on the holiday island and was recently accused by the opposition of abusing his position to get relaxations in building permits for hotels in areas with building restrictions.
The government, which has been tight-lipped on the subject, has not given any indication this was a reason to prompt the cabinet reshuffle.
News of the reshuffle came as no shock to the Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) either, which retreated a mere 19 basis points to settle at 79.91 points.
"The news broke a bit late for us. Besides, the bourse has developed a thick skin," one trader joked.

Clerides's Greek Cypriot administration is recognised as the only legitimate government in Cyprus, which has been divided since Turkey invaded its north in 1974 in response to a brief coup engineered by the colonels ruling in Greece at the time.
